nodes.summary: For every natural number $k \ge 3$, the $k$-generalized Lucas number $L^{(k)}_{2-k}$ equals $0$.
nodes.title: $k$-generalized Lucas numbers at the lowest index

nodes.summary: For every natural number $k \ge 3$ and every integer $n$ with $2 - k \le n \le -1$, the $k$-generalized Lucas number $L^{(k)}_n$ equals $0$.
nodes.title: $k$-generalized Lucas numbers vanish at negative indices

nodes.summary: For every natural number $k \ge 2$, the $k$-generalized Lucas number $L^{(k)}_1$ equals $1$.
nodes.title: $k$-generalized Lucas numbers at index one

nodes.summary: For every natural number $k \ge 2$ and every integer $n \ge 2$, the $k$-generalized Lucas numbers satisfy $L^{(k)}_n = \sum_{i=0}^{k-1} L^{(k)}_{n-k+i}$, that is, $L^{(k)}_n$ is the sum $L^{(k)}_{n-1} + \dots + L^{(k)}_{n-k}$ of the $k$ preceding values.
nodes.title: Recurrence for the $k$-generalized Lucas numbers

nodes.summary: For every natural number $k \ge 2$, the $k$-generalized Lucas number $L^{(k)}_0$ equals $2$.
nodes.title: $k$-generalized Lucas numbers at index zero

nodes.summary: For a natural number $k \ge 2$, the $k$-generalized Lucas numbers $L^{(k)}_n$ are the natural numbers indexed by the integers $n \ge 2 - k$ given by $L^{(k)}_n = 0$ for $2 - k \le n \le -1$, $L^{(k)}_0 = 2$, $L^{(k)}_1 = 1$, and $L^{(k)}_n = L^{(k)}_{n-1} + L^{(k)}_{n-2} + \dots + L^{(k)}_{n-k}$ for every integer $n \ge 2$. No value is assigned at indices below $2 - k$.
nodes.title: $k$-generalized Lucas numbers

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $m$, this is the list $[L^{(n)}_1, \dots, L^{(n)}_m]$ of length $m$ (empty for $m = 0$), where $L^{(n)}_k = 2^k - 1$ for $1 \le k \le n$ and $L^{(n)}_k$ is the sum of the $n$ preceding terms for $k \ge n + 1$. For $n = 0$ every term is $0$.
nodes.title: Finite prefixes of the n-step Lucas numbers

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n \ge 1$ and $m$, the $n$-step Lucas number $L^{(n)}_m$ is defined by $L^{(n)}_0 = 0$, $L^{(n)}_m = 2^m - 1$ for $1 \le m \le n$, and $L^{(n)}_m = \sum_{i=1}^{n} L^{(n)}_{m-i}$ for $m \ge n + 1$. For $n = 0$ we set $L^{(0)}_m = 0$ for every $m$.
nodes.title: n-step Lucas numbers

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
